claim: The inferior parietal lobe (IPL) is a key neural substrate underlying diverse mental processes, from basic attention to language and social cognition.
source: The inferior parietal lobe (IPL) is a key neural substrate underlying diverse mental processes, from basic attention to language and social cognition, that define human interactions.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract as a foundational premise of the study.

claim: The IPL is a heteromodal convergence zone of various brain networks central to realizing key cognitive operations across different levels of the neural processing hierarchy.
source: The inferior parietal lobe (IPL) is a heteromodal convergence zone of various brain networks that is central to realizing key cognitive operations across different levels of the neural processing hierarchy (Kernbach et al., 2018; Seghier, 2013).
evidence: Supported by citations to previous research (Kernbach et al., 2018; Seghier, 2013).

claim: The IPL has probably undergone remarkable expansion and functional reorganization during primate evolution.
source: During primate evolution, the IPL has probably undergone remarkable expansion and functional reorganization (Van Essen and Dierker, 2007; Xu et al., 2020).
evidence: Supported by citations to previous research (Van Essen and Dierker, 2007; Xu et al., 2020).

claim: The emergence of new areas inside the human IPL has been seriously considered.
source: The emergence of new areas inside the human IPL has been seriously considered (Mars et al., 2013), while its precise correspondence to nonhuman homologues is still debated (Seghier, 2013).
evidence: Supported by citations to previous research (Mars et al., 2013; Seghier, 2013).

claim: The right IPL is a key region for visuospatial attention.
source: Systematic reviews have identified the right IPL as a key region for visuospatial attention (Corbetta and Shulman, 2002).
evidence: Supported by citation to previous research (Corbetta and Shulman, 2002).

claim: Neurological damage of the right IPL entails hemi-neglect, the failure to orient visual attention to the contralesional side.
source: Accordingly, neurological damage of the right IPL entails a clinical condition called hemi-neglect: the failure to orient visual attention to the contralesional side (Morrow and Ratcliff, 1998).
evidence: Supported by citation to previous research (Morrow and Ratcliff, 1998).

claim: Language function is widely accepted to lateralize to the (dominant) left hemisphere.
source: In contrast to visuospatial attention, language function is widely accepted to lateralize to the (dominant) left hemisphere (Friederici, 2017).
evidence: Supported by citation to previous research (Friederici, 2017).

claim: Tissue damage to the left temporo-parietal cortex causes impairments of semantic processing.
source: Tissue damage to the left temporo-parietal cortex has been reported, for decades, to cause impairments of semantic processing – key to reading and other elaborate forms of language comprehension (Binder et al., 2009; Hartwigsen et al., 2016; Seghier, 2013).
evidence: Supported by citations to previous research (Binder et al., 2009; Hartwigsen et al., 2016; Seghier, 2013).

claim: There is spatial overlap between semantic and social cognition domains in the left IPL.
source: This view receives support from previous reports on spatial overlap between both cognitive domains in the left IPL (Bzdok et al., 2016; Mars et al., 2011; Seghier, 2013).
evidence: Supported by citations to previous research (Bzdok et al., 2016; Mars et al., 2011; Seghier, 2013).

claim: Advanced social cognitive functions tend to engage the IPL in both hemispheres.
source: However, many human neuroimaging experiments have shown that advanced social cognitive functions, such as the capacity to infer others' thoughts, beliefs, and behavioral dispositions, tend to engage the IPL in both hemispheres (Bzdok et al., 2012; Bzdok et al., 2016).
evidence: Supported by citations to previous research (Bzdok et al., 2012; Bzdok et al., 2016).

claim: The left and right IPL differ on the structural level, indicated by cytoarchitectonic borders and gyral differentiation.
source: Substantiating these earlier hints at functional specialization of left versus right IPL, both regions also differ on the structural level. Architectural heterogeneity is indicated by cytoarchitectonic borders and gyral differentiation (Caspers et al., 2008) as well as anatomical fiber bundle connections as quantified by fiber tractography (Caspers et al., 2011).
evidence: Supported by citations to previous research (Caspers et al., 2008; Caspers et al., 2011).

claim: Structural heterogeneity in the IPL is found between individuals and between the left and right hemisphere.
source: Such heterogeneity in the IPL is not only found between individuals, but also between the left and right hemisphere (Toga and Thompson, 2003).
evidence: Supported by citation to previous research (Toga and Thompson, 2003).

claim: The IPL harbors a major hub of the transmodal association network (default mode network).
source: Finally, the IPL harbors a major hub of the transmodal association network (Braga et al., 2019) ('default mode network') and is densely connected with other cortical key areas for various functions.
evidence: Supported by citation to previous research (Braga et al., 2019).

claim: The attentional reorienting condition significantly modulated neural activity in the right inferior parietal lobes (supramarginal gyrus).
source: Relative to the control condition, we found that the attentional reorienting condition significantly modulated neural activity in several nodes of the default mode network, including the right inferior parietal lobes (IPL) (supramarginal gyrus) and to a lesser extent also the left IPL (supramarginal gyrus), as well as the bilateral precuneus.
evidence: This is a direct result from the study's neural activity analysis.

claim: Real-word processing predominantly activated left-hemispheric parts of the default mode network, including the IPL (angular gyrus).
source: Compared to pseudoword processing, real-word processing predominantly activated left-hemispheric parts of the default mode network, including the IPL (angular gyrus) and middle cingulate gyrus, as well as the superior frontal gyrus.
evidence: This is a direct result from the study's neural activity analysis.

claim: Peak activations for false belief relative to true belief trials encompassed bilateral areas, including the right IPL (angular gyrus).
source: Peak activations for false belief relative to true belief trials (p < 0.001 uncorrected) encompassed bilateral areas, including the supplementary motor cortex, inferior frontal gyrus and precentral gyrus. To a lesser extent, nodes of the default mode network were also engaged, including the left precentral gyrus, right IPL (angular gyrus), and bilateral precuneus.
evidence: This is a direct result from the study's neural activity analysis.

claim: A two-cluster solution was indicated to be optimal in each hemisphere for IPL parcellation.
source: According to the applied cluster validity criteria, a two-cluster solution was indicated to be optimal in each hemisphere considering different cluster numbers. The choice of two final clusters was based on majority votes yielding 97.1% and 78.8% agreement across 25 distinct cluster validity criteria (cf. Materials and methods) for left and right IPL, respectively (Table 1).
evidence: This is a direct result from the study's clustering analysis.

claim: The IPL parcellation procedure led to one anterior subregion and one posterior subregion in each hemisphere.
source: The IPL parcellation procedure led to one anterior subregion (left hemisphere: L-ant, right hemisphere: R-ant) and one posterior subregion (L-post, R-post) in each hemisphere (Figure 2B).
evidence: This is a direct result from the study's parcellation analysis, with reference to Figure 2B.

claim: Around two thirds of the voxels composing the IPL ROI were spatially congruent across hemispheres.
source: Around two thirds of the voxels composing the IPL ROI (left: 64.98%, right: 66.31%) were spatially congruent across hemispheres.
evidence: This is a direct result from the study's hemispheric asymmetry analysis.

claim: Neural activity response patterns from IPL subregions carried relevant information that allowed for successful task classification significantly above chance.
source: Our results indicate that neural activity response patterns from our IPL subregions alone carried relevant information that was granular enough to allow for successful task classification significantly above chance.
evidence: This is a direct result from the study's machine learning analysis.

claim: The logistic predictive model resulted in an overall out-of-sample classification accuracy of 52.11% (chance: 33.33%).
source: The logistic predictive model was cross-validated in a one-versus-rest scheme to attempt classifying trial brain scans from hold-out subjects. This machine learning pipeline resulted in an overall out-of-sample classification accuracy of 52.11% (chance: 33.33%).
evidence: This is a direct result from the study's machine learning analysis.

claim: Increased neural activity in the right anterior subregion and less neural activity in the left anterior subregion was associated with the attentional reorienting task.
source: Relative to the other two experimental tasks, increased neural activity in the right anterior subregion and less neural activity in the left anterior subregion was associated with the attentional reorienting task when considering multivariate patterns distributed across all IPL subregions (see Figure 3).
evidence: This is a direct result from the study's pattern-learning analysis, with reference to Figure 3.

claim: Successful trial classification pertaining to lexical decisions was driven by neural activity increases in the left anterior subregion and neural activity decreases in the right anterior subregion.
source: In contrast, successful trial classification pertaining to lexical decisions was driven by neural activity increases in the left anterior subregion and neural activity decreases in the right anterior subregion, relative to the other two tasks.
evidence: This is a direct result from the study's pattern-learning analysis.

claim: Neural activity within both posterior subregions carried salient information that was instrumental in successfully discriminating trial brain scans recorded during perspective taking.
source: Finally, neural activity within both posterior subregions carried salient information that was instrumental in successfully discriminating trial brain scans recorded during perspective taking.
evidence: This is a direct result from the study's pattern-learning analysis.

claim: The connectivity profiles between the four IPL subregions and large-scale brain networks were significantly different between tasks.
source: The connectivity profiles between the four IPL subregions and large-scale brain networks were significantly different between tasks.
evidence: This is a direct result from the study's functional connectivity analysis.

claim: The anterior subregions showed strong degrees of hemispheric lateralization and domain specificity.
source: The anterior subregions showed strong degrees of hemispheric lateralization and domain specificity.
evidence: This is a direct result from the study's functional connectivity analysis.

claim: The posterior subregions showed less lateralization and a higher degree of across-network coupling.
source: In contrast, the posterior subregions showed less lateralization and a higher degree of across-network coupling.
evidence: This is a direct result from the study's functional connectivity analysis.

claim: During attentional reorienting, the right anterior IPL subregion was stronger involved in cortex-wide connectivity than its left-hemispheric counterpart.
source: During attentional reorienting, the right anterior IPL subregion was stronger involved in cortex-wide connectivity than its left-hemispheric counterpart (Figure 5A, left column; Figure 5D).
evidence: This is a direct result from the study's functional connectivity analysis, with reference to Figure 5A and 5D.

claim: The visual network and regions belonging to the dorsal attention network emerged as preferred coupling partners of the right anterior IPL subregion during attentional reorienting.
source: The visual network and regions belonging to the dorsal attention network emerged as its preferred coupling partners (Figure 4—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is a direct result from the study's functional connectivity analysis, with reference to Figure 4—figure supplement 1.

claim: Attentional reorienting was characterized by a simple coupling configuration, with three significant modulations.
source: Explicitly probing modulatory effects on directed connectivity within the IPL, attentional reorienting was characterized by a simple coupling configuration, with three significant modulations: An increased inhibitory influence from the left anterior to the left posterior subregion, a facilitatory drive from the left posterior to the right anterior subregion, and an inhibitory influence from the right posterior to the right anterior subregion (Figure 5, left).
evidence: This is a direct result from the study's dynamic causal modeling analysis, with reference to Figure 5.

claim: During lexical decisions, strong interhemispheric modulations, both facilitatory and inhibitory, were found between IPL subregions.
source: During lexical decisions, we found strong interhemispheric modulations, both facilitatory and inhibitory, between IPL subregions.
evidence: This is a direct result from the study's dynamic causal modeling analysis.

claim: Task-related connectivity increases from the left anterior subregion to all other subregions were facilitatory during lexical decisions.
source: Strikingly, task-related connectivity increases from the left anterior subregion to all other subregions were facilitatory.
evidence: This is a direct result from the study's dynamic causal modeling analysis.

claim: The right anterior subregion had an inhibitory influence on all other subregions during lexical decisions.
source: In contrast, the right anterior subregion had an inhibitory influence on all other subregions (Figure 5, center).
evidence: This is a direct result from the study's dynamic causal modeling analysis, with reference to Figure 5.

claim: Perspective taking was mainly characterized by increased facilitatory influences between IPL subregions, with the right posterior subregion exerting a facilitatory influence on all other subregions.
source: Perspective taking was mainly characterized by increased facilitatory influences between IPL subregions, with the right posterior subregion exerting a facilitatory influence on all other subregions (Figure 5, right panel).
evidence: This is a direct result from the study's dynamic causal modeling analysis, with reference to Figure 5.

claim: The three cognitive domains of interest were characterized by fundamentally different motifs of effective connectivity modulations among IPL subregions.
source: To summarize, the three cognitive domains of interest were characterized by fundamentally different motifs of effective connectivity modulations among IPL subregions.
evidence: This is a summary conclusion from the study's dynamic causal modeling analysis.

claim: A core observation relies on a simple directed connectivity profile for attentional reorienting and more complex directed connectivity interactions between IPL subregions for both higher-level tasks.
source: A core observation relies on a simple directed connectivity profile for attentional reorienting and more complex directed connectivity interactions between IPL subregions for both higher-level tasks.
evidence: This is a summary conclusion from the study's dynamic causal modeling analysis.

claim: Two distinctable subregions, one anterior and one posterior, were identified per IPL by a functional parcellation analysis based on neural activity estimates for the three cognitive domains.
source: Based on neural activity estimates for the three cognitive domains, two distinctable subregions, one anterior and one posterior, were identified per IPL by a functional parcellation analysis.
evidence: This is a summary of the study's parcellation results.

claim: The right anterior IPL subregion showed the strongest predictive relevance for attentional reorienting.
source: The right anterior IPL subregion showed the strongest predictive relevance for attentional reorienting while the left anterior IPL subregion was strongest associated with semantic processing.
evidence: This is a summary of the study's predictive modeling results.

claim: The left anterior IPL subregion was strongest associated with semantic processing.
source: The right anterior IPL subregion showed the strongest predictive relevance for attentional reorienting while the left anterior IPL subregion was strongest associated with semantic processing.
evidence: This is a summary of the study's predictive modeling results.

claim: Both left and right posterior IPL were robustly engaged when subjects adopted the mental perspectives of others.
source: In contrast, both left and right posterior IPL were robustly engaged when subjects adopted the mental perspectives of others.
evidence: This is a summary of the study's predictive modeling results.

claim: Increased connectivity with diverse large-scale networks was observed with increasing cognitive complexity across tasks.
source: In general, we observed increased connectivity with diverse large-scale networks with increasing cognitive complexity across tasks.
evidence: This is a summary of the study's functional connectivity results.

claim: Global connectivity profiles for the anterior IPL subregions showed strong hemispheric lateralization and domain specificity.
source: Global connectivity profiles for the anterior IPL subregions showed strong hemispheric lateralization and domain specificity.
evidence: This is a summary of the study's functional connectivity results.

claim: Functional connectivity profiles for the left and right posterior subregions were similar within each task and showed a higher degree of across-network coupling.
source: Functional connectivity profiles for the left and right posterior subregions were similar within each task and showed a higher degree of across-network coupling.
evidence: This is a summary of the study's functional connectivity results.

claim: Transient virtual lesions of the right, but not left IPL in the intact human brain were reported to cause performance declines during attentional reorienting.
source: Additionally, transient virtual lesions of the right, but not left IPL in the intact human brain were reported to cause performance declines during attentional reorienting (Rushworth et al., 2001).
evidence: Supported by citation to previous research (Rushworth et al., 2001).

claim: Transient virtual lesions of the left IPL in healthy subjects were reported to disrupt semantic task performance during language comprehension.
source: Consistently, transient virtual lesions of the left IPL in healthy subjects were reported to disrupt semantic task performance during language comprehension (Hartwigsen et al., 2017; Sliwinska et al., 2015).
evidence: Supported by citations to previous research (Hartwigsen et al., 2017; Sliwinska et al., 2015).

claim: A functional dissociation in the specialization of anterior and posterior IPL regions is consistent with findings in non-human primates.
source: A functional dissociation in the specialization of anterior and posterior IPL regions is further consistent with findings in non-human primates (Rozzi et al., 2008).
evidence: Supported by citation to previous research (Rozzi et al., 2008).

claim: Anterior parts of the monkey IPL are functionally specialized in somatosensory processes, whereas posterior parts preferentially process information based on visual input.
source: Anterior parts of the monkey IPL are functionally specialized in somatosensory processes, whereas posterior parts preferentially process information based on visual input (Kravitz et al., 2011).
evidence: Supported by citation to previous research (Kravitz et al., 2011).

claim: The posterior part of the monkey IPL is thought to be particularly involved in navigation, that is, processing one's position in space.
source: The posterior part is thought to be particularly involved in navigation, that is, processing one's position in space (Crowe et al., 2004; Crowe et al., 2005).
evidence: Supported by citations to previous research (Crowe et al., 2004; Crowe et al., 2005).

claim: The IPL expanded in the primate lineage.
source: Notably, the IPL expanded in the primate lineage (Orban et al., 2004), while the existence of a homologue in non-human primate remains uncertain (Mars et al., 2011; Seghier, 2013).
evidence: Supported by citations to previous research (Orban et al., 2004; Mars et al., 2011; Seghier, 2013).

claim: Functional organization reproduces structural organization in unimodal areas in the human brain.
source: As an overarching tendency, functional organization reproduces structural organization in unimodal areas in the human brain.
evidence: This is stated as a general principle in the discussion.

claim: Functional organization is significantly less determined by structure in heteromodal brain regions.
source: In contrast, functional organization is significantly less determined by structure in heteromodal brain regions (Vázquez-Rodríguez et al., 2019).
evidence: Supported by citation to previous research (Vázquez-Rodríguez et al., 2019).

claim: Twenty-two healthy, native German speakers participated in this neuroimaging investigation.
source: Twenty-two healthy, native German speakers (11 female, mean age 27.9 ± 3.28 years) participated in this neuroimaging investigation.
evidence: This is a description of the study sample.

claim: All subjects were right-handed (laterality index ≥80%).
source: All subjects were right-handed (laterality index ≥80% Oldfield, 1971).
evidence: This is a description of the study sample, with citation to the handedness assessment method (Oldfield, 1971).

claim: The functional MRI investigation consisted of three sessions that were performed on separate days, scheduled at least 7 days apart from each other.
source: The functional MRI (fMRI) investigation (see Figure 1—figure supplement 1A) consisted of three sessions that were performed on separate days, scheduled at least 7 days apart from each other.
evidence: This is a description of the experimental design.

claim: Each fMRI session was divided into four runs.
source: Each fMRI session was divided into four runs.
evidence: This is a description of the experimental design.

claim: In all runs, each of the three tasks was administered consecutively in a task block.
source: In all runs, each of the three tasks (i.e. attentional reorienting, lexical decisions, and perspective taking, see below for details) was administered consecutively in a task block.
evidence: This is a description of the experimental design.

claim: The topographical outline for the left and right IPL ROI was guided by the JuBrain probabilistic cytoarchitectonic atlas.
source: The topographical outline for the left and right IPL ROI was guided by an established and freely available histological atlas. Seven cytoarchitectonic maps cover the human IPL in each hemisphere according to the widely used JuBrain probabilistic cytoarchitectonic atlas (Amunts and Zilles, 2001).
evidence: This is a description of the ROI definition method, with citation to the atlas (Amunts and Zilles, 2001).

claim: A k-means clustering was applied at the voxel level with 1000 random centroid initializations based on the estimates from the 'target condition > rest' contrast of the GLMcond in the IPL ROIs.
source: A k-means clustering (Hartigan and Wong, 1979) was applied at the voxel level with 1000 random centroid initializations (Thirion et al., 2014) based on the estimates from the 'target condition > rest' contrast of the GLMcond in the IPL ROIs.
evidence: This is a description of the clustering method, with citations to the algorithm (Hartigan and Wong, 1979) and initialization approach (Thirion et al., 2014).

claim: The unsupervised clustering algorithm was applied on pooled information across subjects and separately for each hemisphere.
source: The unsupervised clustering algorithm was applied on pooled information across subjects and separately for each hemisphere.
evidence: This is a description of the clustering method.

claim: 74 voxels in the left and 84 in the right IPL ROI were removed from the final solution because their cluster assignments were unstable across the random centroid initializations of the k-means algorithm.
source: For all later analysis steps, 74 (out of 1102) voxels in the left and 84 (out of 1123) in the right IPL ROI were removed from the final solution because their cluster assignments were unstable across the random centroid initializations of the k-means algorithm.
evidence: This is a description of the data processing step.

claim: The Schaefer-Yeo atlas with 400 parcels was used to parse the distributed neural activity estimates.
source: We drew on the commonly used Schaefer-Yeo atlas v0.15.3 (Schaefer et al., 2018) with 400 parcels to parse the distributed neural activity estimates (GLMtrial) of the three target conditions (invalid, word, false belief).
evidence: This is a description of the functional connectivity analysis method, with citation to the atlas (Schaefer et al., 2018).

claim: A fully connected DCM (full model) estimated all possible connections among the four IPL subregions (including self-connections) and directions of modulatory influences.
source: A fully connected DCM (full model) estimated all possible connections among the four IPL subregions (including self-connections) and directions of modulatory influences.
evidence: This is a description of the DCM analysis method.

claim: Subject-wise full models were optimized for the intrinsic connections (A matrix) and modulatory inputs (B matrix) at the group level using the Bayesian model selection procedure.
source: After model estimation, subject-wise full models were optimized for the intrinsic connections (A matrix) and modulatory inputs (B matrix) at the group level using the Bayesian model selection procedure (Friston and Penny, 2011).
evidence: This is a description of the DCM analysis method, with citation to the optimization procedure (Friston and Penny, 2011).

claim: A non-parametric permutation test on subject-wise parameters of the optimal reduced model identified those model parameters that varied significantly between tasks.
source: As a second-level random-effects analysis, we conducted a non-parametric permutation test on subject-wise parameters of the optimal reduced model. This layer of analysis identified those model parameters that varied significantly between tasks.
evidence: This is a description of the DCM analysis method.

claim: Statistical significance was determined based on the absolute parameter difference higher than 99.9% of the baseline difference, corresponding to α ≤ 0.01.
source: Statistical significance was determined based on the absolute parameter difference higher than 99.9% of the baseline difference, corresponding to α ≤ 0.01.
evidence: This is a description of the statistical testing method.

claim: The study was performed according to the guidelines of the Declaration of Helsinki and approved by the Ethics Committee of the Medical Faculty of the University of Leipzig, Germany.
source: The study was performed according to the guidelines of the Declaration of Helsinki and approved by the Ethics Committee of the Medical Faculty of the University of Leipzig, Germany.
evidence: This is a statement about ethical approval.

claim: Written informed consent was obtained from all subjects before the experiment.
source: Written informed consent was obtained from all subjects before the experiment.
evidence: This is a statement about ethical procedures.

claim: All tasks showed increased neural activity in a widespread set of brain regions, including the IPL.
source: In this analysis, all tasks showed increased neural activity in a widespread set of brain regions, including the IPL.
evidence: This is a summary of the neural activity analysis results.

claim: The attentional reorienting condition significantly modulated neural activity in the left IPL (supramarginal gyrus) to a lesser extent than the right IPL.
source: Relative to the control condition, we found that the attentional reorienting condition significantly modulated neural activity in several nodes of the default mode network, including the right inferior parietal lobes (IPL) (supramarginal gyrus) and to a lesser extent also the left IPL (supramarginal gyrus), as well as the bilateral precuneus.
evidence: This is a direct result from the study's neural activity analysis.

claim: Key nodes of the dorsal attention network were activated during attentional reorienting, including the left frontal eye field and superior parietal lobe.
source: Key nodes of the dorsal attention network were also activated, including the left frontal eye field and superior parietal lobe.
evidence: This is a direct result from the study's neural activity analysis.

claim: The results for the social cognition task were less strong than for the other tasks.
source: As expected, the results for the social cognition task were less strong (Rothmayr et al., 2011; Sommer et al., 2010).
evidence: This is a statement about the strength of results, with citations to previous research (Rothmayr et al., 2011; Sommer et al., 2010).

claim: The three-cluster solution emerged as the second best choice for IPL parcellation (left IPL: 2.8% agreement, right IPL: 21.2% agreement).
source: The three-cluster solution emerged as the second best choice (left IPL: 2.8% agreement, right IPL: 21.2% agreement).
evidence: This is a result from the cluster validity analysis.

claim: The task-dependent BOLD responses from the model that explicitly accounts for general motor responses across tasks (GLMcond+RT) closely resembled the results from the original analysis.
source: This reaction time regressor captured unspecific motor preparation and execution components that were not of interest here. The task-dependent BOLD responses closely resembled the results from the original analysis (Figure 2—figure supplement 2).
evidence: This is a result from the control analysis, with reference to Figure 2—figure supplement 2.

claim: 95.3% and 73.0% of the majority votes selected a two cluster solution for the left and right IPL respectively, based on GLMcond+RT.
source: The data-driven clustering based on these results selected a similar parcellation solution with comparable certainty. 95.3% and 73.0% of the majority votes selected a two cluster solution for the left and right IPL respectively, based on GLMcond+RT.
evidence: This is a result from the control analysis.

claim: 82 voxels in the left IPL and 73 in the right IPL were unstable across random initializations in the GLMcond+RT parcellation.
source: 82 voxels in the left IPL and 73 in the right IPL were unstable across random initializations.
evidence: This is a result from the control analysis.

claim: Subregion-specific across-hemisphere congruency was nearly perfect (L-ant: 88.97%; L-post: 100%; R-ant: 100%; R-post: 93.48%).
source: Considering these corresponding voxels contained in both left and right IPL ROI, subregion-specific across-hemisphere congruency was nearly perfect (L-ant: 88.97%; L-post: 100%; R-ant: 100%; R-post: 93.48%).
evidence: This is a result from the hemispheric symmetry analysis.

claim: Appropriately balanced numbers of trials were ensured for all conditions by sub-sampling to the minimum number of trials per subject and fMRI run.
source: This modeling strategy naturally yielded a set of predictive weights for all subregions for each task. Appropriately balanced numbers of trials were ensured for all conditions by sub-sampling to the minimum number of trials per subject and fMRI run.
evidence: This is a description of the data processing method.

claim: Signal deconfounding removed variation that could be explained by session number, session time, subject identify, or run time.
source: Signal deconfounding removed variation that could be explained by session number, session time, subject identify, or run time.
evidence: This is a description of the data processing method.

claim: A run-wise variable standardization was applied by de-meaning to zero and unit-variance scaling to one.
source: A run-wise variable standardization was applied, before model estimation, by de-meaning to zero and unit-variance scaling to one.
evidence: This is a description of the data processing method.

claim: The generalization performance of the prediction accuracy was estimated via leave-one-subject-out cross-validation.
source: The generalization performance of the prediction accuracy was estimated via leave-one-subject-out cross-validation.
evidence: This is a description of the validation method.

claim: 22 model instances were built from the brain data so that each subject's data were held out once from the training process and exclusively used to assess the model's generalization properties.
source: In total, 22 model instances were built from the brain data so that each subject's data were held out once from the training process ('training') and exclusively used to assess the model's generalization properties ('testing').
evidence: This is a description of the cross-validation method.

claim: The parameters of the predictive algorithm were averaged across all cross-validation folds to guard against noise and obtain a single aggregate predictive model solution for inspection and visualization.
source: The parameters of the predictive algorithm were averaged across all cross-validation folds to guard against noise and obtain a single aggregate predictive model solution for inspection and visualization (Kernbach et al., 2018).
evidence: This is a description of the model aggregation method, with citation to previous work (Kernbach et al., 2018).

claim: For each experimental target condition, Pearson's correlation coefficients were computed between a given IPL subregion and each of the Schaefer-Yeo parcels.
source: For each experimental target condition, Pearson's correlation coefficients were computed between a given IPL subregion and each of the Schaefer-Yeo parcels.
evidence: This is a description of the functional connectivity analysis method.

claim: Task-specific functional coupling shifts were determined by statistical significance testing based on a non-parametric permutation procedure using an empirical null-hypothesis distribution.
source: Task-specific functional coupling shifts were determined by statistical significance testing based on a non-parametric permutation procedure using an empirical null-hypothesis distribution (Bzdok et al., 2019; Bzdok and Yeo, 2017).
evidence: This is a description of the statistical testing method, with citations to previous work (Bzdok et al., 2019; Bzdok and Yeo, 2017).

claim: Subject-specific node centers per subregion were based on the peak activity across all three tasks.
source: Subject-specific node centers per subregion were based on the peak activity across all three tasks.
evidence: This is a description of the DCM node definition method.

claim: Task-wise normalization of neural activity estimates was performed to ensure similar contribution of all tasks in defining the subject-wise DCM nodes.
source: We ensured similar contribution of all tasks by task-wise normalization of neural activity estimates to define the subject-wise DCM nodes.
evidence: This is a description of the data processing method.

claim: The first eigenvariate from the timeseries of voxels in an 8 mm sphere around the target was extracted for DCM analysis.
source: The first eigenvariate from the timeseries of voxels in an 8 mm sphere around this target was extracted (Zeidman et al., 2019).
evidence: This is a description of the DCM data extraction method, with citation to previous work (Zeidman et al., 2019).

claim: Only data from voxels within the upper quartile of estimated neural activity were included to ensure functional relevance.
source: We exclusively included data from voxels within the upper quartile of estimated neural activity to ensure functional relevance (Seghier and Friston, 2013) and assured that all voxels fell into the respective IPL subregion.
evidence: This is a description of the data selection method, with citation to previous work (Seghier and Friston, 2013).

claim: The trial onsets of the three target conditions were modeled as direct inputs to the nodes and as modulatory inputs to the inter-regional connections.
source: The trial onsets of the three target conditions were modeled as direct inputs to the nodes and as modulatory inputs to the inter-regional connections.
evidence: This is a description of the DCM modeling approach.

claim: Neural activity stemming from incorrect trials and control conditions was regressed out in the DCM analysis.
source: Neural activity stemming from incorrect trials and control conditions was regressed out (Zeidman et al., 2019).
evidence: This is a description of the data processing method, with citation to previous work (Zeidman et al., 2019).

claim: The optimized, reduced model represented fixed-effects at the group level.
source: The optimized, reduced model represented fixed-effects at the group level (Rosa et al., 2012).
evidence: This is a description of the DCM model, with citation to previous work (Rosa et al., 2012).

claim: For each task, the parameter differences of the remaining two tasks were randomly shuffled 10,000 times to obtain and test against an empirical distribution for the null hypothesis.
source: Specifically, for each task, the parameter differences of the remaining two tasks were randomly shuffled 10,000 times to obtain and test against an empirical distribution for the null hypothesis (i.e., no differences between task-dependent effective connectivity).
evidence: This is a description of the permutation testing method.

claim: The left anterior subregion was less engaged in cortical connectivity during attentional reorienting, and showed the strongest coupling with the dorsal attention network and the fronto-parietal control network.
source: The left anterior subregion was less engaged in cortical connectivity, and showed the strongest coupling with the dorsal attention network and the fronto-parietal control network.
evidence: This is a result from the functional connectivity analysis.

claim: Compared to the other two functional domains, lexical decisions led to less cortex-wide connectivity, most strongly with left hemispheric dorsal attention network regions.
source: Compared to the other two functional domains, lexical decisions led to less cortex-wide connectivity, most strongly with left hemispheric dorsal attention network regions.
evidence: This is a result from the functional connectivity analysis.

claim: The perspective taking connectivity profiles for the left and right anterior subregions showed coupling with various networks, revealing the strongest coupling patterns with left-hemispheric default mode network and bilateral fronto-parietal control network regions.
source: In contrast, the perspective taking connectivity profiles for the left and right anterior subregions showed coupling with various networks. These IPL subregions revealed the strongest coupling patterns with left-hemispheric default mode network and bilateral fronto-parietal control network regions.
evidence: This is a result from the functional connectivity analysis.

claim: During attentional reorienting, specific cortical connectivity shifts emerged for the right posterior subregion rather than the left posterior subregion of the IPL ROI.
source: During attentional reorienting, specific cortical connectivity shifts emerged for the right posterior subregion rather than the left posterior subregion of the IPL ROI (Figure 5A, right column; Figure 5D).
evidence: This is a result from the functional connectivity analysis, with reference to Figure 5A and 5D.

claim: Attentional reorienting led to significantly enhanced functional coupling of the right posterior subregion with the visual network and left-hemispheric parts of the somatomotor network, as well as increased connectivity with right-hemispheric parts of the fronto-parietal control network.
source: Relative to the other two tasks, attentional reorienting led to significantly enhanced functional coupling with the visual network and left-hemispheric parts of the somatomotor network, as well as increased connectivity with right-hemispheric parts of the fronto-parietal control network (Figure 4—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is a result from the functional connectivity analysis, with reference to Figure 4—figure supplement 1.

claim: Processing lexical decisions was specifically characterized by coherent connectivity increases between the posterior IPL subregions and the bilateral visual network, the default mode network and the ventral attention network.
source: Processing lexical decisions in turn was specifically characterized by coherent connectivity increases between the posterior IPL subregions and the bilateral visual network, the default mode network and the ventral attention network.
evidence: This is a result from the functional connectivity analysis.

claim: Engagement in perspective taking engendered significantly stronger functional connectivity for the left posterior subregion and extended parts of several large-scale brain networks.
source: Finally, engagement in perspective taking engendered significantly stronger functional connectivity for the left posterior subregion and extended parts of several large-scale brain networks.
evidence: This is a result from the functional connectivity analysis.

claim: While the left posterior subregion showed similar connectivity strength to bilateral parts of large-scale networks during perspective taking, the right posterior subregion mainly interacted with contralateral parts.
source: While the left posterior subregion showed similar connectivity strength to bilateral parts of large-scale networks, the right posterior subregion mainly interacted with contralateral parts.
evidence: This is a result from the functional connectivity analysis.

claim: The posterior IPL regions showed connectivity links with multiple coupling partners, including regions belonging to the visual network, to the ventral and dorsal attention network, and to the somatomotor network during perspective taking.
source: The posterior IPL regions showed connectivity links with multiple coupling partners, including regions belonging to the visual network, to the ventral and dorsal attention network, and to the somatomotor network.
evidence: This is a result from the functional connectivity analysis.

claim: The DCM optimization procedure provided one Bayesian parameter average group-level model.
source: The DCM optimization procedure provided one Bayesian parameter average group-level model.
evidence: This is a description of the DCM analysis result.

claim: All modulatory parameters of the optimal DCM model exceeded zero given a 95% confidence interval.
source: All modulatory parameters of this optimal model exceeded zero given a 95% confidence interval.
evidence: This is a result from the DCM analysis.

claim: Interhemispheric interactions between subregions were mainly facilitatory during perspective taking.
source: Interhemispheric interactions between subregions were also mainly facilitatory during perspective taking (Figure 5, left).
evidence: This is a result from the DCM analysis, with reference to Figure 5.

claim: The attention coupling topology was distinctively closer to the intrinsic connectivity than effective modulation patterns underlying both other domains.
source: The attention coupling topology was distinctively closer to the intrinsic connectivity than effective modulation patterns underlying both other domains.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the DCM results.

claim: The relatively automatic lexical decision task was specifically associated with the left anterior IPL cluster, while the more complex perspective taking task was specifically associated with both posterior IPL subregions.
source: The relatively automatic lexical decision task in the present study was specifically associated with our left anterior IPL cluster, while the more complex perspective taking task was specifically associated with both posterior IPL subregions.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the study's results in the context of previous research.

claim: The functional connectivity analysis demonstrated relatively stronger across-network coupling with several cortical networks for the posterior IPL cluster.
source: Consistently, our functional connectivity analysis demonstrated relatively stronger across-network coupling with several cortical networks for our posterior IPL cluster.
evidence: This is a summary of the functional connectivity results.

claim: The monkey-human homologue of IPL anatomy remains insufficiently understood.
source: It is, however, important to bear in mind that the monkey-human homologue of IPL anatomy remains insufficiently understood (Mars et al., 2013; Seghier, 2013).
evidence: Supported by citations to previous research (Mars et al., 2013; Seghier, 2013).

claim: A high degree of abstraction from sensory information in the macaque IPL is substantiated by the existence of intention- and goal-specific neurons rather than pure movement-coding neurons.
source: A high degree of abstraction from sensory information in the macaque IPL is further substantiated by the existence of intention- and goal-specific neurons rather than pure movement-coding neurons in the macaque IPL (Fogassi et al., 2005; Rozzi et al., 2008).
evidence: Supported by citations to previous research (Fogassi et al., 2005; Rozzi et al., 2008).

claim: The existence of a homologue of the human IPL in non-human primate remains uncertain.
source: Notably, the IPL expanded in the primate lineage (Orban et al., 2004), while the existence of a homologue in non-human primate remains uncertain (Mars et al., 2011; Seghier, 2013).
evidence: Supported by citations to previous research (Mars et al., 2011; Seghier, 2013).

claim: The expansion of the IPL may relate to cognitive capacities which are unique to humans, including the ability for speech and language processing as well as complex problem solving.
source: The expansion of the IPL may relate to cognitive capacities which are unique to humans, including the ability for speech and language processing as well as complex problem solving.
evidence: This is a speculative statement based on the evolutionary context.

claim: The study confirms and details the previously reported gradient in the complexity of processing in the human IPL, which likely reflects fine-tuned functional differentiation for higher cognitive operations in humans.
source: We confirm and detail the previously reported gradient in the complexity of processing in the human IPL, which likely reflects fine-tuned functional differentiation for higher cognitive operations in humans.
evidence: This is a summary conclusion integrating the study's results with previous research.

claim: Distinct functional specialization for human-defining cognitive operations in the IPL may explain differences in the connectivity profiles of the larger IPL regions between humans and macaques.
source: Distinct functional specialization for human-defining cognitive operations in the IPL may explain differences in the connectivity profiles of the larger IPL regions between humans and macaques (e.g. Margulies et al., 2016; Oligschläger et al., 2019; Xu et al., 2020).
evidence: This is a speculative statement supported by citations to previous research (Margulies et al., 2016; Oligschläger et al., 2019; Xu et al., 2020).

claim: Functional organization is significantly less determined by structure in heteromodal association areas, including the IPL.
source: Such laxer coupling of structure-function relations is observed in heteromodal association areas, including the IPL (Margulies et al., 2016).
evidence: Supported by citation to previous research (Margulies et al., 2016).

claim: Functional specialization for higher cognitive operations may gradually decouple from the underlying structure.
source: In general, functional specialization for higher cognitive operations may gradually decouple from the underlying structure (Vázquez-Rodríguez et al., 2019).
evidence: Supported by citation to previous research (Vázquez-Rodríguez et al., 2019).

claim: The functional parcellation does not simply follow cytoarchitectonic boundaries.
source: This notion is in line with the present results from our functional parcellation which does not simply follow cytoarchitectonic boundaries.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the study's parcellation results.

claim: For relatively low-level cognitive processes, task-specific coupling adjustment implicated a reduced set of coupling partners.
source: For relatively low-level cognitive processes, here exemplified by attentional reorienting, task-specific coupling adjustment implicated a reduced set of coupling partners.
evidence: This is a summary of the effective connectivity results.

claim: For more complex tasks, more elaborate coupling motifs were found, including dense intra- and inter-hemispheric facilitation and inhibition.
source: In contrast, for more complex tasks, as exemplified by lexical decision and perspective taking, we found evidence for more elaborate coupling motifs, including dense intra- and inter-hemispheric facilitation and inhibition.
evidence: This is a summary of the effective connectivity results.

claim: There is a scarcity of existing studies directly devoted to investigating the left and right IPL in several different psychological tasks.
source: Notably, there is a scarcity of existing studies directly devoted to investigating the left and right IPL in several different psychological tasks.
evidence: This is a statement about the state of the literature.

claim: The few existing studies committed to the effective connectivity of the IPL mainly focused on task-related connectivity changes between an IPL subregion and other areas of a specialized network for a single cognitive domain, typically in one hemisphere only.
source: The few existing studies committed to the effective connectivity of the IPL mainly focused on task-related connectivity changes between an IPL subregion and other areas of a specialized network for a single cognitive domain, typically in one hemisphere only (Fukuda et al., 2019; Hartwigsen et al., 2017).
evidence: Supported by citations to previous research (Fukuda et al., 2019; Hartwigsen et al., 2017).

claim: Task-induced shifts in functional connectivity revealed key distinctions in interactions with major brain networks.
source: Task-induced shifts in functional connectivity revealed key distinctions in interactions with major brain networks.
evidence: This is a summary of the functional connectivity results.

claim: Functional coupling profiles varied significantly between the three experimental tasks.
source: Functional coupling profiles varied significantly between the three experimental tasks.
evidence: This is a summary of the functional connectivity results.

claim: Across domains, coupling partners were recruited from various large-scale brain networks.
source: Across domains, coupling partners were recruited from various large-scale brain networks.
evidence: This is a summary of the functional connectivity results.

claim: The observation reinforces the notion of the IPL interfacing multiple neural systems and different levels of neurocognitive abstraction.
source: Our observation reinforces the notion of the IPL interfacing multiple neural systems and different levels of neurocognitive abstraction (Bzdok et al., 2013; Seghier, 2013).
evidence: This is an interpretation of the results, supported by citations to previous research (Bzdok et al., 2013; Seghier, 2013).

claim: The task-specific coupling profiles between IPL subregions and a variety of cortical partners are anchored in the functional compartments uncovered in the IPL.
source: Moreover, we show that the task-specific coupling profiles between IPL subregions and a variety of cortical partners are anchored in the functional compartments uncovered in the IPL.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the results.

claim: The hemisphere-specific functional coupling for the anterior IPL subregions is broadly consistent with the common reports of right-hemispheric specialization of attentional reorienting processes and left-hemispheric specialization for semantic processes.
source: The hemisphere-specific functional coupling for the anterior IPL subregions is broadly consistent with the common reports of right-hemispheric specialization of attentional reorienting processes (Rushworth et al., 2001; Schuwerk et al., 2017) and left-hemispheric specialization for semantic processes (Binder et al., 2009; Braga et al., 2019; Hartwigsen et al., 2016).
evidence: This is an interpretation of the results, supported by citations to previous research (Rushworth et al., 2001; Schuwerk et al., 2017; Binder et al., 2009; Braga et al., 2019; Hartwigsen et al., 2016).

claim: The rich connectivity profiles of the left and right posterior IPL subregions support the notion of bilateral IPL relevance for social cognitive processes.
source: The rich connectivity profiles of the left and right posterior IPL subregions support the notion of bilateral IPL relevance for social cognitive processes, consolidating previous findings (Bzdok et al., 2013; Bzdok et al., 2016).
evidence: This is an interpretation of the results, supported by citations to previous research (Bzdok et al., 2013; Bzdok et al., 2016).

claim: During attentional processing, the dedicated coupling partners of the right anterior IPL subregion included regions of the visual cortex and the dorsal attention network.
source: Specifically, during attentional processing, the dedicated coupling partners of the right anterior IPL subregion included regions of the visual cortex and the dorsal attention network.
evidence: This is a summary of the functional connectivity results.

claim: During semantic processing, the left anterior subregion enhanced coupling with regions of the default mode and ventral attention network.
source: During semantic processing, the left anterior subregion enhanced coupling with regions of the default mode and ventral attention network.
evidence: This is a summary of the functional connectivity results.

claim: During social cognition processing, the left and right posterior IPL subregions preferably coupled with the default mode network.
source: Ultimately, during social cognition processing, the left and right posterior IPL subregions preferably coupled with the default mode network.
evidence: This is a summary of the functional connectivity results.

claim: The observed task-specific functional coupling of the posterior subregions with major brain networks was largely symmetric across both hemispheres.
source: The observed task-specific functional coupling of the posterior subregions with major brain networks was largely symmetric across both hemispheres.
evidence: This is a summary of the functional connectivity results.

claim: The study provides evidence for a functional triple dissociation in the human IPL, with task-specific functional specialization in distinct IPL subregions.
source: To summarize our integrated experimental and computational study, we provide evidence for a functional triple dissociation in the human IPL, with task-specific functional specialization in distinct IPL subregions.
evidence: This is a summary conclusion of the study.

claim: The emerging view of functional triple dissociation is supported by information carried in precise multivariate predictive signatures.
source: This emerging view is supported by information carried in precise multivariate predictive signatures.
evidence: This is a summary conclusion of the study.

claim: The effective connectivity analyses revealed that attentional reorienting mediated simpler coupling modulations, while semantic and social cognition were realized by more complex inter-hemispheric influences.
source: Zooming into task-specific coupling motifs among IPL subregions, our effective connectivity analyses revealed that attentional reorienting mediated simpler coupling modulations, while semantic and social cognition were realized by more complex inter-hemispheric influences.
evidence: This is a summary conclusion of the study.

claim: The posterior IPL subregions were linked to bilateral, symmetric recruitment of distributed cortical coupling partners, reminiscent of the default mode network.
source: Delineating task-evoked shifts in functional coupling patterns, in turn, uncovered that the posterior IPL subregions were linked to bilateral, symmetric recruitment of distributed cortical coupling partners, reminiscent of the default mode network.
evidence: This is a summary conclusion of the study.

claim: The anterior IPL subregions were engaged in flexible and hemisphere-specific coupling patterns with brain-wide cortical partners.
source: Conversely, the anterior IPL subregions were engaged in flexible and hemisphere-specific coupling patterns with brain-wide cortical partners.
evidence: This is a summary conclusion of the study.

claim: The results shed new light on how currently under-appreciated activity and connectivity profiles within the left and right IPL support some of the most distinctive mental capacities in humans.
source: Together, our results shed new light on how currently under-appreciated activity and connectivity profiles within the left and right IPL support some of the most distinctive mental capacities in humans.
evidence: This is the overarching conclusion of the study.
